mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 3% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which negatively impacts earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a decrease in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 0.2% month-over-month jointly indicate accelerating labor market weakness, which reduces consumer demand and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month AND PAYEMS < previous month by > 0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by more than 0.2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 900,000 units, combined with a concurrent drop in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals a broad-based collapse in residential demand and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both HOUST falls below 900,000 and GDPC1 declines month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of stable federal funds rates near zero, combined with rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL), signals a low-for-long monetary regime with eroding real yields, which historically supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS unchanged at 0% for 12 months AND CPIAUCSL > previous year
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is at zero for 12 months and CPIAUCSL is rising year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS rising above its 5-year average for six consecutive months) signals elevated precautionary behavior, which typically precedes a consumer spending rebound and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS is above its 5-year average for six consecutive months.
